summary: fix(mirror): stamp parent_id on cached mutation responses by threading the request path into writeMutationResponseToStore
reason: Follow-up to mirror-canonical-resource-name (Copilot review of PR #9, internal/cli/data_source.go:479). That patch canonicalised the resource name in writeMutationResponseToStore but left the upsert unstamped, because the function was not given the request path. For a parent-keyed resource (purchases, sales, journal_entries, bank_accounts, ... every entry in resourceParentKeyColumns whose parent column is parent_id) resourceStorageID then fell back to a BARE id, which reintroduces both halves of the original bug for rows written by a mutation: (a) loadCompanyResources filters on $.parent_id, so a cached mutation row was invisible to every detector and rollup, and (b) two companies' entities carrying the same API id collided on the resources primary key (resource_type, id) and the later write destroyed the earlier one. The fix mirrors writeThroughCache exactly: the generated mutation commands already hold the substituted API path in their local `path` variable, so it is passed as a fifth argument and writeMutationResponseToStore calls mirrorWithParentID(items, mirrorCompanySlugFromPath(requestPath)) before UpsertBatch. The generated-file edit is one argument plus a two-line PATCH comment at each of the 67 mutation call sites; no other generated logic changes. A path that carries no company slug (/companies, /user, an unsubstituted {companySlug} template) yields an empty slug and mirrorWithParentID passes the items through untouched, so account-level resources keep the bare id that is their correct storage key.
call_sites: func writeMutationResponseToStore(ctx context.Context, resourceType string, data json.RawMessage, responsePath string, requestPath string) {
validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test -count=1 ./... pass. New hand-authored tests in internal/cli/mirror_canonical_test.go: TestWriteMutationResponseToStore_StampsParentIDFromRequestPath (a simulated purchase mutation response for two different company slugs produces the two storage keys 4242\0agensia and 4242\0other-co instead of one bare 4242 row, and loadCompanyResources(agensia) sees exactly the agensia row), TestWriteMutationResponseToStore_NoSlugKeepsBareKey (a /companies mutation keeps the bare slug key), and TestGeneratedMutationCallSitesPassRequestPath, which scans every generated file in internal/cli and fails if any writeMutationResponseToStore call site does not pass the `path` variable -- that scan, not the representative needles in call_sites[], is what makes a reprint fail closed across all 67 sites. No API call was made; the tests write to a temporary HOME.
